answer.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are funnel-mechanics problems, and the inherited record points twice at onboarding/signup friction (memory_86, memory_31) as a durable lever. That is also the direction most aligned with the stated objective: friction removal grows qualified revenue without buying it. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the tempting answer to the competitor, but discount-led acquisition is exactly where reported 'revenue lift' can mask downstream value erosion — worse cohort quality, margin compression, and churn that lands outside the original measurement window. I want the archived record for memory_73 specifically to see whether retention and revenue quality were tracked past the promo period or only acquisition and top-line. I want memory_86 because memory_86 and memory_31 may be the same underlying experiment consolidated twice; if so, the apparent double confirmation for onboarding is one data point, not two, and my confidence should drop accordingly. I am also treating all of these as day 12–61 summaries of archived records: the environment has changed (a new competitor exists that did not exist when these were run), so prior effect sizes are directional, not predictive. Referral incentive (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) address neither of the two declining metrics this week. Committing at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout, with first-week activation as the primary metric and cohort retention as an explicit guardrail — if verification shows memory_86 and memory_31 are duplicates, I would downgrade to a small guarded test rather than switch directions.
